transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-13
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Horizon Procurement), Devon Price (Horizon CISO), Luke Moreno (Horizon Cloud)

Summary:
Quick workshop to decide SLA escalation path, reconcile DPA redlines, and align on pilot acceptance criteria. Primary tension: Horizon wants strict egress/data residency + delegated KMS; procurement needs a clear escalation ladder if SLOs slip.

Topics: SLA tiers, incident escalation, DPA clauses (data residency, subprocessor list), KMS/HSM options, Dedicated vs Hosted cost/latency tradeoffs, pilot acceptance gates.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're gonna do a quick run through on the sla escalation flow and the dpa points you flagged, i'll pause for questions as we go - sound good?
[00:00:25] Marta (Horizon): yep that's perfect, appreciate you squeezing this in today. procurement is under a tight window so we want clarity on what happens if latency or availability dips below agreed sros.
[00:00:45] Devon (Horizon): and from security, the main ask is customer-managed keys or an HSM-backed KMS, plus audit logs that survive retention windows for 7 years - i know that's a lot.
[00:01:10] Priya (Redwood): totally understood. quick note: we support KMS integrations and a pegged privileged-key flow for Dedicated/private deployments; hosted does support CMEK in some regions but there's an implementation timeline.
[00:01:38] Alex (Redwood): also to frame the escalation ladder: first tier is automatic alerting and costless mitigation (auto-scaling, route to variant), second tier is priority support + SLA credit, third is exec escalation. we'll walk the language in the SLA doc.
[00:02:05] Luke (Horizon): can you clarify what "route to variant" means? if you divert to a smaller model is that considered a service degradation for us?
[00:02:28] Priya (Redwood): good question. by default routing to a compatible variant is an operational fallback to preserve availability; the SLA has explicit clauses on quality degradation vs availability — we can flag that with your product team.
[00:02:52] Marta (Horizon): procurement needs firm numeric SLOs and a transparent formula for credits. last time i saw a vendor had a weird exception for maintenance windows. we want maintenance windows scheduled and notified 72 hours in advance.
[00:03:15] Alex (Redwood): we can add maintenance carve-outs with minimum notice windows; 72 hours is acceptable for planned work, emergency maintenance would still have an agreed communication protocol.
[00:03:38] Devon (Horizon): what about data residency — our policy says EU data at rest for EU customers, and logs containing PII can't leave the region. does Redwood hosted offer region-locked storage for logs?
[00:03:59] Priya (Redwood): hosted supports region pinning for inference in certain regions; log retention/residency can be configured with our enterprise package or Dedicated where logs remain in your VPC for Private deployment. slight hesitation: some telemetry for product monitoring may still be processed in control plane regions unless you choose the Private control plane.
[00:04:28] Luke (Horizon): so Dedicated looks attractive from residency and KMS perspective, but procurement will push back on committed dollars. do you have recommended pilots that limit spend?
[00:04:46] Alex (Redwood): yes, we typically recommend a hybrid pilot: start Hosted with pinned-region and CMEK for smoke tests, then shift critical routing for production to Dedicated once you sign a capacity commit. that gives procurement a lower initial cost.
[00:05:10] Marta (Horizon): can you quantify latency and cost difference? we have a 200 qps burst profile and 99th percentile latency targets under 120ms for simple text-generation flows.
[00:05:31] Priya (Redwood): rough thumb: Dedicated on equivalent GPUs tends to shave 10-30% off p99 latency for medium-length sequences because of sustained batching and lower noisy neighbor risk; cost per token depends on utilization and commit discounts — we'll run a detailed sim for your 200 qps profile.
[00:05:57] Devon (Horizon): and security posture: do you provide SOC2 and ISO attestation and pen test reports? our legal wants to see that before signing.
[00:06:12] Alex (Redwood): yes we can share SOC 2 and ISO docs; we'll include redacted pen test summaries. for DPA we have standard clauses but we can review the specific redlines you submitted.
[00:06:33] Marta (Horizon): in the DPA we asked to strike the broad subprocessor clause and require notification and opt-out; is that a dealbreaker?
[00:06:50] Priya (Redwood): we can be transparent about subprocessors; the standard is notification and a mechanism to object to high risk subprocessors — we can't practically remove all subprocessors, but we can give you a process for escalation and, for private deployments, you can limit third-party telemetry.
[00:07:12] Luke (Horizon): regarding retention, we want 7 year audit log retention for certain classes of events. what's your default and how customizable is it?
[00:07:29] Alex (Redwood): default hosted retention is 90 days for request-level logs; enterprise packages allow extended retention and log export to your S3 or GCS bucket. for Dedicated/Private you can configure retention to 7 years within your environment.
[00:07:52] Devon (Horizon): ok so it sounds like Dedicated ticks a lot of security boxes, but cost is the hangup. procurement wants a clear SLA escalation path that doesn't rely on credits only — they want temporary capacity increases or prioritized routing as remediation.
[00:08:17] Priya (Redwood): we do have burst capacity and prioritized routing as part of Dedicated plans. in the SLA we can enumerate remediation options: capacity burst, priority provisioning, and if those fail, financial credits. we can also offer runbook-driven incident responses with named engineers.
[00:08:43] Marta (Horizon): can you add a clause that during incidents you'll provide a 1-hour response for Sev1s and a 4-hour remediation window for network/throughput issues? procurement likes hard numbers.
[00:09:04] Alex (Redwood): 1-hour response for Sev1 is feasible as a premium SLA; remediation windows depend on scope but we can put a target of 4 hours for certain categories — we'll map categories to response/remediation times in the SLA matrix.
[00:09:26] Luke (Horizon): on KMS: is bring-your-own-key supported for Hosted in our target region? or do we have to do Dedicated?
[00:09:40] Priya (Redwood): CMEK support in hosted is region-dependent; for full BYOK and HSM-backed workflows, Dedicated or Private control plane is the straightforward path. Hosted with CMEK may meet your needs for initial pilot if the region supports it.
[00:10:05] Devon (Horizon): another legal question: the DPA's indemnity clause currently has a broad cap tied to fees; we usually ask to tie cap to a fixed multiple or carve out certain breach types. is that open for negotiation?
[00:10:24] Alex (Redwood): indemnity caps are something we negotiate usually; we'll surface options: standard cap, higher cap for enterprise with exceptions, and carve-outs for willful misconduct. we'll mark that for legal follow-up.
[00:10:44] Marta (Horizon): procurement also asked about data subject requests and support for deletion workflows — who is responsible for executing deletions if data is in logs retained by Redwood?
[00:11:00] Priya (Redwood): we have DSR support via API for hosted and full control for Dedicated/Private; we can include SLA'd timelines for fulfilling DSRs in the DPA.
[00:11:20] Alex (Redwood): i'm going to share a draft SLA matrix today and a DPA with redlines highlighted; let's use those as the working artifacts.
[00:11:34] Marta (Horizon): great. one more procurement question: billing and egress charges — if we keep logs in-region, are there still outbound egress fees when we export to our bucket?
[00:11:51] Priya (Redwood): export to your bucket in the same region shouldn't incur provider egress, but cross-region exports might. we'll add egress scenarios to the pricing annex.
[00:12:14] Devon (Horizon): i want to confirm we can get a dedicated runbook with contact points and an on-call rotation for the pilot. procurement will likely want that tied to SLA.
[00:12:27] Alex (Redwood): yes named on-call and runbook are standard for enterprise pilots; we'll include response rosters.
[00:12:43] Luke (Horizon): switching topics briefly, we need to know if Redwood provides a private control plane for EU-only customers. that's a requirement for one of our business units.
[00:12:58] Priya (Redwood): we do offer a private control plane for enterprise customers; it's part of Private deployments and can be air-gapped in certain cases — we'll get the architecture note to you.
[00:13:17] Marta (Horizon): procurement timeline is end of May for approval. can you commit to deliver the updated docs so we can iterate?
[00:13:29] Alex (Redwood): yes we'll aim for the 18th for SLA and DPA updates.
[00:13:40] [silence/typing 00:13:40-00:15:00]
[00:15:02] Priya (Redwood): i want to run through a few technical clarifications — Luke can you describe the 200 qps profile in a bit more detail? mean vs peak, sequence lengths, and concurrency.
[00:15:20] Luke (Horizon): average is 40 qps sustained with bursts to 200 qps during business hours; typical sequence length is short (prompt+20 tokens), a small percentage of long-form requests for reports. concurrency varies by user activity patterns.
[00:15:45] Priya (Redwood): thanks; that helps. for short sequences we can optimize batching aggressivly, but bursts will need warm pools in Dedicated to meet p99 targets. for hosted we'd recommend a warmup script as part of the pilot.
[00:16:08] Devon (Horizon): any concerns about prefix caching or KV cache leaking PII? we need assurances that cache eviction and encryption are audited.
[00:16:25] Priya (Redwood): caches are encrypted at rest in our systems, and KV caches can be isolated per-customer on Dedicated. we'll include the cache handling section in the security appendix.
[00:16:40] Alex (Redwood): circling back to escalation: if we put the three-tier ladder into the SLA, procurement also wants a transparent timeline for credits and a runbook that proves attempts to remediate. does that sound right?
[00:16:58] Marta (Horizon): yes exactly, and also a point where if remediation fails repeatedly we can terminate with a reduced notice period.
[00:17:12] Alex (Redwood): termination for repeated breach is negotiable; we'll propose thresholds (e.g., more than 3 Sev1 breaches in a quarter) and corresponding remedies.
[00:17:28] [00:17:28 - 00:30:00 - extended technical discussion condensed]
[00:30:05] Alex (Redwood): okay quick recap of what we'll produce: updated SLA matrix with numeric SLOs and escalation times; DPA with subprocessors list and a proposed opt-out/notification process; architecture note on private control plane and KMS options; pilot plan for hybrid hosted -> Dedicated path; cost sim for your 200 qps traffic.
[00:30:30] Marta (Horizon): good, procurement needs the SLA matrix to include notice windows, response times, remediation windows and a clear credit formula.
[00:30:45] Priya (Redwood): noted - we'll make those explicit. also adding named contact rosters and on-call SLAs.
[00:31:02] Luke (Horizon): can you include an example incident timeline and a sample post-incident report template? that will help security sign-off.
[00:31:18] Alex (Redwood): yes we'll attach a PIR template.
[00:31:30] Devon (Horizon): lastly, legal wants to see a limited set of acceptance tests for the pilot — basic perf, data residency verification, and DSR fulfillment test. can Redwood support that?
[00:31:46] Priya (Redwood): absolutely, we can run a joint acceptance test plan and provide logs/audit proof for residency.
[00:32:00] Marta (Horizon): procurement will need the pricing annex to show committed vs burst costs and a simple break-even for Dedicated commit levels.
[00:32:16] Alex (Redwood): we'll provide a pricing annex and cost/break-even analysis.
[00:32:30] [short side conversations and clarifications 00:32:30-00:45:00]
[00:45:05] Alex (Redwood): ok closing round — any final blockers?
[00:45:12] Marta (Horizon): legal is watching the indemnity cap and subprocessors clause. procurement wants the escalation ladder and maintenance notice windows. security wants KMS options and the PIR template.
[00:45:30] Devon (Horizon): and we need assurance about log residency during pilot.
[00:45:38] Alex (Redwood): all noted, we'll consolidate and send updated artifacts by the 18th.
[00:45:50] Marta (Horizon): thanks, that works. we'll plan a follow-up for the week of the 21st to validate the pilot acceptance tests.
[00:46:02] Alex (Redwood): perfect, thanks everyone.
